parsed.headline: Advance voting for Toronto’s 2026 municipal election begins September 29

pages.text: Advance voting for the 2026 municipal election in Toronto, Canada, is scheduled to begin on September 29, 2026. According to the City of Toronto, advance voting will take place from September 29 to October 6, and from October 4 to October 11, between the hours of 10 a.m. and 7 p.m. The city is offering two voting locations in each of its 25 wards, and eligible voters may choose to vote at either location within their specific ward. To be eligible to vote, a person must reside in the ward where they cast their ballot, and individuals may only vote once regardless of how many properties they own or rent in the city. Advance voting turnout data is scheduled to be released in a news release on October 13, following the Monday, October 12 holiday.

Voters who have requested to vote by mail must return their completed mail-in voting packages, including marked ballots and supporting documents, to Toronto Elections by noon on September 30, 2026. Packages can be returned via 25 secure, yellow Toronto Elections drop boxes located throughout the city, with one box situated in each ward. These boxes are monitored by CCTV, inspected regularly, and emptied daily by election staff. The City’s Media Attendance at a Voting Place policy will remain in effect during the advance voting period and on election day, October 26.

parsed.headline: Supreme Court of Canada Chief Justice stresses need to protect democratic institutions

pages.text: Chief Justice Richard Wagner stated that Canada's democratic institutions require protection against unrelenting pressures as the Supreme Court of Canada opened a new judicial year. Speaking at a ceremony on Monday, Wagner noted that the world is experiencing increasing uncertainty driven by deepening polarization, the rapid emergence of artificial intelligence, and a non-stop pace of events. He compared democratic institutions and the rule of law to an anchor, stating that their strength is measured during a storm rather than in calm waters. 1.  The ceremony took place at the West Memorial Building, which serves as the court's temporary location near Parliament Hill while its permanent home undergoes renovations expected to last at least 10 years. 2.  Justice Minister Sean Fraser addressed the courtroom of dignitaries, noting that provinces, communities, and various groups are questioning their roles within the Canadian federation. Fraser stated that preserving national unity requires improving public belief that existing systems serve their interests and noted the law's role in this process. 3.  A formal welcome for the court's newest member, Glenn Joyal, is scheduled to occur next month.

parsed.headline: UN Secretary General calls for permanent Gaza ceasefire

pages.text: United Nations Secretary General Antonio Guterres called for a permanent ceasefire in Gaza on October 5, 2026, ahead of the third anniversary of the October 7, 2023, Hamas attack on Israel. In a statement, Guterres called for a “political path to lasting peace across the whole region,” stating that it is time to allow humanitarian assistance at scale and respect international law. He noted that a brief ceasefire announced by US President Donald Trump in October 2025 “brought some relief,” but argued it has not delivered security, adequate humanitarian assistance, or a credible path to recovery and peace. According to the Palestinian Health Ministry, which is under Hamas’ authority and deemed reliable by the UN, Israel’s military campaign in Gaza has killed more than 74,200 people. Guterres acknowledged the October 7, 2023, attack was “abhorrent,” resulting in the deaths of more than 1,200 Israelis and foreign nationals and the taking of 251 hostages. He also noted that Palestinians in Gaza have faced “massive loss of life, displacement and destruction.”

parsed.headline: President of Bangladesh calls for transparency and accountability from chartered accountants

pages.text: President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir called on chartered accountants to operate with professionalism and integrity to ensure accountability and transparency within Bangladesh's institutional sector. Speaking on Monday, the President stated that audit professionals and chartered accountants hold a vital role in sustaining investor confidence and maintaining financial discipline across state-owned, private, and public organisations. These remarks were made during an afternoon meeting at Bangabhaban with a six-member delegation from the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Bangladesh (ICAB), led by ICAB President Sabbir Ahmed. During the meeting, the delegation briefed the President on the organisation's activities and invited him to serve as the chief guest at an international conference scheduled for November, organised by the South Asian Federation of Accountants (SAFA). The President accepted the invitation and assured the delegation of his participation. The meeting was attended by the President's secretaries and other relevant senior officials.

parsed.headline: Reporters discuss potential impact of Iran war on US midterm elections

pages.text: On September 29, 2026, The Guardian World hosted a live Q&A session to discuss how the war with Iran might affect US voters and the political landscape ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. As the war enters its eighth month, reporters addressed questions regarding its implications for US foreign policy, government spending, and personal finances, as well as the potential political consequences for Donald Trump and other candidates running in November. The session featured senior political correspondent Lauren Gambino, political breaking news reporter Joseph Gedeon, global affairs correspondent Andrew Roth, data editor Will Craft, and political correspondent Robert Tait.

parsed.headline: Bangladesh and World Bank sign $300 million deal for food security project

pages.text: The Government of Bangladesh and the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank Group signed a financing agreement on Monday to implement the “Emergency Support for Food Security Project.” According to an Economic Relations Division (ERD) press release, the agreement is for 219,200,000.00 Special Drawing Rights (SDR), equivalent to $300.00 million. The project aims to support food security by ensuring the availability of eligible fertilizers, specifically for smallholder farmers, during planting seasons. The scheduled implementation period for the project is from July 1, 2026, to June 30, 2027. The agreement was signed by Shahriar Kader Siddiky, Secretary of the Economic Relations Division (ERD) within the Ministry of Finance, and Jean Pesme, the World Bank Division Director for Bangladesh and Bhutan. Implementation will be managed by the Finance Division (FD) in coordination with the Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC) and the Bangladesh Chemical Industries Corporation (BCIC). The loan features a 25-year maturity period, which includes a five-year grace period, and carries an interest rate of 1.5% per annum on the withdrawn credit balance. While the loan includes a maximum commitment fee of up to 0.50% per annum on the unwithdrawn financing balance, the World Bank has been waiving the commitment fee for Bangladesh for many years, including the current fiscal year.

parsed.headline: Yemen's internationally recognized government launches military operation to retake Houthi-held areas

pages.text: On October 4, 2026, Yemen’s Saudi-backed, internationally recognized government launched a major military operation aimed at retaking areas controlled by the Houthis. Rashad al-Alimi, President of the Yemeni Presidential Leadership Council, stated in a televised address that government forces would continue operations until Houthi control is ended. Al-Alimi noted the decision to launch the offensive followed the exhaustion of efforts to reduce tensions and called on regional and international partners to support the council's institutions. The offensive follows recent Houthi gains in strategic highlands near Taiz, which brought the group closer to the last road linking Taiz with the government seat in Aden. According to the AFP news agency, more than 70 people were reportedly killed in fighting around Taiz over the past day. The Yemeni military reported that operations were commencing in the Houthi-held capital, Sanaa, while allied forces reportedly retook the town of Dhubab north of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Simultaneously, the Saudi-led coalition reported hitting Houthi military targets in Hodeida on the Red Sea coast, with a coalition spokesman stating naval forces destroyed weapons depots, facilities for booby-trapped boats and naval mines, and thwarted a planned attack on southern Red Sea waterways.

The escalation included retaliatory strikes from the Houthis. A Houthi military spokesman stated the group launched ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco facilities in Riyadh and the Khurais area, as well as King Khalid International Airport and an oil refinery in the Red Sea city of Rabigh. The Houthis claimed these attacks were in response to approximately 50 air and missile strikes carried out by the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen over the previous 12 hours. Saudi Arabia had not immediately commented to confirm the reported strikes. Regarding international involvement, regional and Western officials told Reuters that Saudi Arabia and Yemeni allies were preparing the operation, with Riyadh expected to conduct air operations and Yemeni forces conducting ground operations. Six sources familiar with preparations indicated the United States is providing intelligence to support Saudi operations, while regional and European countries are providing military assistance focused mainly on defense. Additionally, Turkey and Pakistan agreed to deploy troops as part of the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement signed with Saudi Arabia in August.

parsed.headline: Hydro One purchase of 145-year-old Toronto heritage home may lead to demolition

pages.text: A 145-year-old heritage home near Kensington Market in Toronto, Canada, may face demolition following its purchase earlier this year by the utility company Hydro One. The building, located at 28-30 Cecil Street, was constructed in 1881 and has been on the city’s heritage register for 50 years. It sits adjacent to a Hydro One transformer station that is scheduled for expansion to meet increasing electricity demands. In a statement to CBC Toronto, the utility company said the station requires updated equipment and additional capacity to maintain reliability and support the city's growing needs. While Hydro One declined to comment on specific plans for the home, a utility staff member noted in a Sept. 28 letter to Member of Provincial Parliament Jessica Bell that the company is unable to retain the existing building for its station plans.

The potential demolition has drawn opposition from approximately 20 tenants facing eviction and local residents. George Traini of the Baldwin Village Community Association suggested that preserving the building's facade would be the best outcome for the neighborhood. Adam Wynne, chair of the Toronto and East York Community Preservation Panel, expressed being disheartened by the takeover and is calling on the province to allow municipalities more time to research and nominate listed properties for full heritage designation. Under the province’s 2022 More Homes Built Faster Act, municipalities must promote listed properties to full heritage designation by Jan. 1, 2027, or the properties will be removed from the heritage register and become open to development.
